chunks: My father narrated to me, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Zayyat, from Karam, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him say: Verily, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed in anguish. And it is fitting for Allah that no one who comes to him in anguish returns except that Allah sends him back pleased.

key_terms.حَقِيقٌ: fitting or obligatory by divine attribute

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of visiting Imam Husayn's shrine for someone in grief?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) as a state of profound distress (makrub), from which God guarantees the relief of those who visit his shrine. This narration, found in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, underscores the theological principle that the Ahl al-Bayt serve as intercessors who transform the grief of their devotees into divine joy, reinforcing the spiritual efficacy of Ziyarah in Shia piety.
